content.text: The visible suite now passes (3 passed). I changed one file, `solution/core.py`. The cause was operand order in the binary operators. The code did `a, b = pop(), pop()`, which put the top of the stack in `a` and the value below it in `b`, so every operator worked on its arguments backwards. That's why `PUSH 1, PUSH 2, LT` gave 0, why `DIV`/`MOD` checked the wrong operand for zero and never raised `VMZeroDivision`, and why `SUB` in the countdown loop computed `1 - x` instead of `x - 1`, so the loop never reached zero and hit the step limit. Changing it to `b, a = pop(), pop()` fixes all three failures. I also fixed a related bug no visible test covers: `SWAP` pushed its two values back in their original order, so it did nothing. It now actually swaps them, and I confirmed that `PUSH 1, PUSH 2, SWAP` gives `[2, 1]`. One thing I left alone: `DIV` uses Python's floor division, so negative results round down rather than toward zero. No test or spec says which is intended.

result: The visible suite now passes (3 passed). I changed one file, `solution/core.py`. The cause was operand order in the binary operators. The code did `a, b = pop(), pop()`, which put the top of the stack in `a` and the value below it in `b`, so every operator worked on its arguments backwards. That's why `PUSH 1, PUSH 2, LT` gave 0, why `DIV`/`MOD` checked the wrong operand for zero and never raised `VMZeroDivision`, and why `SUB` in the countdown loop computed `1 - x` instead of `x - 1`, so the loop never reached zero and hit the step limit. Changing it to `b, a = pop(), pop()` fixes all three failures. I also fixed a related bug no visible test covers: `SWAP` pushed its two values back in their original order, so it did nothing. It now actually swaps them, and I confirmed that `PUSH 1, PUSH 2, SWAP` gives `[2, 1]`. One thing I left alone: `DIV` uses Python's floor division, so negative results round down rather than toward zero. No test or spec says which is intended.
